text:
alex: Heads-up — after the runtime deploy yesterday (attention-optim + kernel selector changes) we saw a ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on a couple of customer workloads (gpt-3-like). Happening on both S1 and S2 pools. Attaching quick numbers below.

tessa: ugh. rough numbers?

ryan: quick snapshot from perf job:```
Before deploy: prefix_hit=0.76, avg_tok_latency=12.0ms, p95_latency=42ms
After deploy:  prefix_hit=0.62, avg_tok_latency=16.5ms, p95_latency=59ms
Requests sampled: 120k
Cache evictions spiked around deploy time.
```

mina: can we confirm whether cache keying changed? iirc we recently added compile flags into the exec-context hash to avoid mismatches across kernels. that could accidentally change prefix keys if namespace not isolated.

alex: good call. grep'd logs for cache keys and found kernel/compile metadata leaking into the prefix key namespace. example key (redacted):
```
model=v2|prefix_sha=3a7f2b|exec_shape=1x2048|kernel=attn_opt_v2|quant_profile=aq_8bit_v3
```

ryan: exact. commit 9f4a2b9 added `exec_metadata` into a generic `cache_key()` helper. we used it for execution cache but the prefix_key wrapper ended up calling the same helper. bad assumption.

tessa: so prefixes that were temperature-insensitive are now siloed across kernels/quant profiles and can't hit each others' entries. that explains lower hit-rate and higher latency.

mina: two paths: (A) quick revert to stop including exec metadata in prefix keys, or (B) adapt warmup to include kernel/quant variants (expensive but correct). I'd prefer A + rewarm.

alex: agree. also we should audit what fields are in the prefix key. suggested canonical prefix key fields: `model_version`, `prefix_sha`, `prefix_length`, `client_tenant` (optional). nothing about kernel/quant/compile flags.

ryan: opened PR to remove exec_metadata from prefix_key: https://git.internal/r/infra/commit/abc123 (draft). I'll add unit tests to assert prefix keys are stable across kernel builds.

perf-bot: perf/regression alert: job=prefix-cache-hit-rate, delta=-18%, ci-run=1782054300

alex: next steps I propose:
- roll patch to revert key leak (ryan)
- schedule a distributed prewarm job for top-100 prefixes across S1/S2 (tessa)
- add regression test in perf harness to ensure prefix hit-rate doesn't regress >5% after kernel/quant changes (mina)
- add CI gating so compile/kernel changes require a cheap synthetic prewarm check (alex)

tessa: prewarm script exists: `tools/prewarm/prefix_prewarm.py` — we should extend it to take `--variant all` to hit kernel/quant combos if we need to. for immediate fix we'll run variant=default after revert. command: `./tools/prewarm/prefix_prewarm.py --pool S1 --top 100 --concurrency 50`

ryan: patch is ready for review. i'll also add a small script to detect when prefix keys contain exec metadata: `rg "kernel=|quant_profile=" -- cache_dump | head`

mina: longer term: we should decouple prefix cache from execution cache in code (separate stores/namespaces). also consider a compacted key format like `sha(prefix)+model+tenant` to be explicit.

alex: agree. add an item to eng-runtime backlog for 'cache key hygiene & namespace separation'.

tessa: I'll kick off the prewarm after revert lands. estimate 45m to repopulate hot prefixes for sampled workloads.

ryan: rolling out revert to canary now. deploy-bot status?

deploy-bot: deploy 1782054400 by ryan — canary to S1 completed at 2026-03-10T12:34:00Z, no errors.

alex: monitoring live metrics. initial canary shows prefix_hit up from 0.62 -> 0.74 in that shard. still a little short of original 0.76 but trending.

perf-bot: quick follow-up: run `perf/compare --metric prefix_hit --before 1782054200 --after 1782054500` and post results.

ryan: will run full perf compare and paste results in incident ticket. opening: INC-2026-042 (prefix cache regression after attn-opt/kernel selector tweak).

mina: also adding unit test: `test_prefix_key_stability` that iterates over kernel variants and asserts identical prefix keys for identical prefix/model/tenant inputs.

tessa: thumbs up. ping me when prewarm starts so I can watch the warmup logs (:eyes:).

alex: thanks team — big win if revert + prewarm gets us back to pre-deploy hit-rates. we'll follow up with the backlog item to avoid repeat.
